Purchase.title: Purchase
Purchase.description: Represents a purchase of INRTX-reserve tokens.

id.description: Unique identifier for the purchase record.

wallet.description: The wallet address of the user who made the purchase.

chainId.description: The chain ID of the network used for the purchase (e.g., 137 for Polygon).

paymentToken.description: The token used for payment ('USDT' or 'POL').

tokensRequested.description: The number of INRTX-reserve tokens requested.

usdPerToken.description: The USD price per INRTX-reserve token at the time of purchase.

usdSubtotal.description: The total USD value of the purchase.

currencyAmountPaid.description: The amount of currency (USDT or POL/MATIC) paid for the purchase.

txHash.description: The transaction hash of the purchase (can be null until the real transaction occurs).

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the purchase record was created (server timestamp).

SaleStats.title: SaleStats
SaleStats.description: Represents aggregated statistics for the token sale.

id.description: Unique identifier for the sale statistics record. Should only ever be one.

totalTokensSold.description: The total number of INRTX-reserve tokens sold.

totalBuyers.description: The total number of unique buyers.

totalUsdtCollected.description: The total amount of USDT collected.

totalPolMaticCollected.description: The total amount of POL/MATIC collected.

usdEquivalentCollected.description: The total USD equivalent value collected from all sources.

Config.title: Config
Config.description: Represents configuration values for the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the configuration record. Should only ever be one.

saleCap.description: The maximum number of INRTX-reserve tokens that can be sold.

usdtAddress.description: The address of the USDT token contract on Polygon.

priceApiUrl.description: The URL of the API used to fetch the POL/MATIC price in USD.

refreshInterval.description: The interval (in seconds) at which to refresh data.

definition.description: Stores individual purchase records. Only authenticated users can create records. Includes denormalized 'wallet' for indexing/querying.

params.name: purchaseId
params.description: The unique identifier for the purchase document.

definition.description: Stores aggregated statistics for the token sale. Requires admin role to modify.

params.name: statsId
params.description: The unique identifier for the sale statistics document (should only be one).

definition.description: Stores configuration values for the application. Requires admin role to modify.

params.name: configId
params.description: The unique identifier for the configuration document (should only be one).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be simple and secure, focusing on ease of querying and clear security rules. All data is stored in top-level collections for easy access and management.  Since there are no user specific subcollections, path based authorization is not necessary. 

*   `purchases`: Stores individual purchase records.  Authorization Independence is ensured as only authenticated users can create purchase records.  Rules ensure server timestamps only.
*   `sale_stats`: Stores aggregated statistics for the token sale. There should only ever be one record. Requires admin role to modify.
*   `config`: Stores configuration values for the application such as the sale cap and API URLs. There should only ever be one record. Requires admin role to modify.

This structure facilitates secure `list` operations (QAPs) as each collection has a homogeneous security posture.  There is no need for complex filtering in rules; the rules are simple and straightforward.

There is no need for nested collections or complex authorization logic, resulting in a simple, easy to debug, secure, and scalable solution.
